stories.title: Nominations Are Open for Connect CRE’s 2026 Women in Real Estate Awards
stories.excerpt: Nominations are open for the 10th consecutive year of Connect CRE’s Women in Real Estate Awards. We will honor women whose talent, drive, leadership and fresh ideas have helped them succeed and become influential in commercial real estate. We invite you to participate in selecting this year’s honorees. We’ll put the spotlight on women from each of the 11 regions we cover with daily news. From coast to coast, that means honorees from California; Seattle and the Pacific Northwest; Phoenix and the Southwest; Texas; Chicago and the Midwest; Boston and New England; New York and Tri-State; Washington, DC; Atlanta and the Southeast; and Florida and the Gulf Coast, as well as National honorees.  Along with nominees from across the country, we’re also looking across the CRE spectrum. Last year’s honorees included women in brokerage, finance, development, investment, asset management and real estate law, among other disciplines that were represented. After considering your recommendations, we’ll choose this year’s honorees. We’ll begin announcing them in October. The deadline for nominations is Friday, Sept. 11. The post Nominations Are Open for Connect CRE’s 2026 Women in Real Estate Awards appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Connect CRE announces 10th annual Women in Real Estate Awards across 11 U.S. regions.
Nominations open for honorees in brokerage, finance, development, investment, and asset management.
Announcements begin October 2026; regional and national winners recognized.
stories.summary: Connect CRE is accepting nominations for its 2026 Women in Real Estate Awards, recognizing female leaders across 11 regions and multiple CRE disciplines. Winners will be announced beginning in October 2026. This is the 10th consecutive year of the awards program.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development fundamentals. This is an industry recognition program with no bearing on demand, supply, capital, or construction costs.

stories.title: Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Varia US Properties AG, the Swiss-listed investor in the U.S. multifamily sector, externally managed by Stoneweg, an SWI Group Company, has formed a US$693.9 million two-vehicle joint venture with affiliates of Brookfield Asset Management for 13 of Varia’s 17-property U.S. multifamily portfolio. The JV provides access to up to US$200 million equity capital to fund future acquisitions, enabling Varia US to expand its portfolio and reposition the Company towards a higher-quality portfolio. Varia US will actively invest in the JV assets to maximize value ahead of planned disposals. Comprising 4,112 units across nine U.S. states, the 13 properties have been divided into two newly formed vehicles, with an aggregate gross asset value of approximately $694 million. Four properties will remain wholly owned and consolidated by Varia US. Max-Herve George, co-founder and CEO of SWI Group, said, “This joint venture gives us the firepower and the flexibility to concentrate on high-quality residential communities, while positioning Varia US to grow decisively as the U.S. living sector continues to reward scale and discipline.” Pictured: Varia US’ Rolling Hills Apartments in Louisville, KY. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Varia US, Brookfield Launch $694M Multifamily Joint Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Varia US and Brookfield form $694M JV covering 13 properties, 4,112 units across nine states.
JV unlocks $200M equity capital for future multifamily acquisitions and portfolio repositioning.
Varia retains 4 properties; JV structure enables high-quality portfolio concentration and disposals.
stories.summary: Swiss-listed Varia US and Brookfield Asset Management have launched a $693.9 million joint venture encompassing 13 multifamily properties totaling 4,112 units across nine states. The structure provides up to $200 million in equity capital to fund acquisitions and reposition Varia toward higher-quality assets. Varia retains four properties wholly owned.
stories.impact: Capital formation and sponsor partnerships are tightening around scale and quality; smaller, fragmented portfolios face pressure to consolidate or reposition. This signals disciplined capital focusing on institutional-grade assets, raising competition for mid-tier development sites and indicating cap-rate compression for trophy properties. Varia's emphasis on "high-quality" suggests weaker assets in secondary markets face headwinds.

stories.title: Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease
stories.excerpt: Logistics Plus has signed a 744,452-square-foot industrial lease in the southern Dallas suburb of Wilmer. The Pennsylvania-based provider of freight and fulfillment services will occupy the entire Building 2 within the Southport Logistics Center, an approximately 1.5 million-square-foot development. Building 2 features 123 dock doors, three drive-in doors and 4,647 square feet of speculative office space. Building 1, still vacant, includes 121 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 389 car parking spaces, 170 trailer parking spaces, and 3,534 square feet of speculative office space. Kurt Griffin and Nathan Orbin of JLL represented the landlord, a joint venture between Bandera Ventures and Invesco Real Estate, in the lease negotiations. In addition to the Wilmer site, Logistics Plus has another warehouse in Haslet. The facilities have a combined 2 million square feet of storage space in the region. Logistics Plus has over 12 million square feet of commercial warehouse space across North America. The post Logistics Plus Signs 744K-SF Wilmer Warehouse Lease appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Logistics Plus leases 744K SF in Wilmer (south Dallas) from Bandera/Invesco joint venture.
Southport Logistics Center is 1.5M SF development; Building 1 remains vacant.
Logistics Plus operates 2M SF combined in Dallas-Wilmer area; 12M SF North America-wide.
stories.summary: Pennsylvania-based freight and fulfillment provider Logistics Plus signed a 744,452-square-foot industrial lease for the entire Building 2 at Southport Logistics Center in Wilmer, south Dallas. Building 1 (750K SF) remains vacant. Logistics Plus now operates 2 million combined square feet in the region.
stories.impact: Moderate multifamily relevance: strong industrial absorption in south Dallas (Wilmer) signals robust logistics and distribution demand, supporting job growth and worker in-migration to outer-ring suburbs. This validates demand for workforce and affordable multifamily product in South Dallas submarkets. However, Building 1 vacancy and speculative office space indicate soft conditions for some asset classes, so developers should focus on retail-trade and last-mile logistics employment centers for rent-growth synergies.

stories.title: Data Center Supplier Inks 196K-SF Lease in Hutto
stories.excerpt: Partners Real Estate represented AI Prefab Solutions, a Texas-based critical-infrastructure manufacturer, in its lease of a new 196,523-sq.-ft. Class A facility in Hutto, Texas. The facility, known as Innovation 8, stretches just under three football fields in length and will serve as the company’s headquarters and primary manufacturing site, with its first system entering production in September 2026. Partners Real Estate’s Stan Nowak and Andrew Alizzi led the assignment on behalf of AI Prefab Solutions, which designs, builds, integrates, and factory-tests prefabricated modular power solutions that bring hyperscale data centers and semiconductor facilities online faster, safer, and more reliably. Innovation Business Park is a Hutto industrial development anchored by major corporate neighbors and expanding infrastructure. Demand for advanced manufacturing and critical infrastructure space has grown alongside the AI compute buildout across Central Texas, where well-located industrial product remains in short supply. AI Prefab Solutions plans to add 200 to 300 full-time employees by 2028. The post Data Center Supplier Inks 196K-SF Lease in Hutto appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AI Prefab Solutions leases 196.5K SF in Hutto, Texas; HQ and manufacturing for data-center power systems.
Tenant plans 200–300 FTE additions by 2028; first production September 2026.
Demand for advanced manufacturing space growing with AI compute buildout; industrial supply tight in Central Texas.
stories.summary: AI Prefab Solutions, a Texas manufacturer of prefabricated power solutions for hyperscale data centers and semiconductors, leased a 196,523-square-foot Class A facility in Hutto as its headquarters and primary manufacturing site. The company projects 200 to 300 full-time hires by 2028, with first-system production starting September 2026. Demand for advanced manufacturing is strong amid Central Texas's AI compute expansion.
stories.impact: AI-driven industrial and semiconductor ecosystem growth in Central Texas (Austin metro, Hutto submarket) is seeding major employment clusters. This signals sustained in-migration of high-skill workers and supporting service labor, validating immediate-term multifamily development targeting both executive and workforce housing around tech manufacturing corridors. Tight industrial supply and infrastructure expansion confirm that submarkets anchoring data-center and semiconductor supply chains will outperform regionally for apartment demand and rent growth.

stories.title: ASU Adding Hotel to its Main Street Entertainment District
stories.excerpt: Arizona State University is adding an upscale hotel in the heart of its Main Street entertainment district. Novus Innovation Corridor will be the site for a seven-story, 116,855-square-foot property that will be part of Marriott Bonvoy’s Tribute Portfolio. The hotel will feature 168 guest rooms, a rooftop pool and bar, and a 2,700-square-foot meeting space. Okland Construction will oversee the hotel’s planning, design and construction management. Sports venue-anchored mixed-use districts are getting national attention for their ability to attract people and increase the value of surrounding properties, and Novus is a leading collegiate example.  ASU is investing more than $150 million in sports venues at Novus, including $55 million in an indoor football practice facility and another $100 million for the modernization of the university’s 51-year-old Desert Financial Arena. That’s on top of the $300 million renovation of Mountain America Stadium and the resounding success of the $140 million, 5,000-seat Mullett Arena.  The post ASU Adding Hotel to its Main Street Entertainment District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Arizona State University building 168-room Marriott Tribute Portfolio hotel in Novus Innovation Corridor, Tempe.
ASU investing $150M+ in Novus sports venues (football, arena, stadium); $300M+ capital total.
Seven-story, 116.8K SF hotel with rooftop bar, 2.7K SF meeting space; Okland Construction managing.
Sports venue-anchored mixed-use showing national success in attracting foot traffic and property values.
stories.summary: Arizona State University is developing a 168-room, seven-story Marriott Bonvoy Tribute Portfolio hotel at its Novus Innovation Corridor in Tempe. The $116,855-square-foot property will include rooftop pool, bar, and meeting space. ASU is investing over $150 million in Novus sports infrastructure—including an indoor football facility, Desert Financial Arena modernization, Mountain America Stadium renovation, and Mullett Arena—as part of a larger $300+ million capital program.
stories.impact: University-anchored mixed-use with sports venue density signals strong experiential demand and extended-stay capture in Tempe. Heavy institutional capital backing real estate creates spillover rental demand: visiting families, recruits, athletes' relatives, and event attendees drive hotel and short-term rental segments, while sustained foot traffic supports ground-floor retail, F&B, and entertainment. For multifamily developers: Novus's success validates mixed-income, mixed-use product near college campuses and validates build-to-suit opportunities in university real estate nodes. Tempe's supply pipeline may tighten if construction labor and capital concentrate on Novus; premium multifamily near campus will benefit from halo effect and absorption.

stories.title: S3 Capital Lends $35M for Miami-Dade County Apartments
stories.excerpt: Miami developer Aconcagua Group has landed $35 million of construction financing to complete a multifamily project in Miami-Dade County, Commercial Observer has learned. S3 Capital provided the loan for the third and final phase of the 374-unit Casa Princeton apartment community in Princeton, Fla. The deal closed Friday morning. The phase three portion of the development will comprise an eight-story building with 162 apartments. The second phase Casa Princeton, encompassing 150 units, was delivered in March 2026 and is roughly 40 percent leased, according to S3. “Casa Princeton speaks directly to the attainable housing gap we’re seeing in markets across Florida,” Steven Jemal, managing director of origination at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “The absorption of the initial phases has validated the underlying demand for the product, which gives us conviction as a lender.” Berkadia negotiated the debt with a Miami-based team consisting of Charles Foschini and Christopher Apone. Located at 12835 SW 246th Terrace 30 miles south of Downtown Miami, the apartment community features one and two-bedroom floorplans. Community amenities include a clubhouse, event space, co-working areas, swimming pool, fitness center, playground and dog park. “The Live Local program is a practical example of public policy helping experienced developers deliver more housing where it is needed,” Robert Schwartz, managing principal at S3 Capital, said in a statement. “We’re proud to participate in public-private partnership programs like this, which make it economically possible to increase limited housing supplies and generate value for local communities, developers and our own stakeholders.” Aconcagua Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: S3 Capital lends $35M construction financing to Aconcagua Group for Casa Princeton Phase 3 (Miami-Dade).
Phase 3: 162 units, eight-story building; Phase 2 (150 units, delivered March 2026) ~40% leased.
Full project: 374 units; lender cites validation of attainable housing demand and phase absorption.
stories.summary: Miami-based Aconcagua Group secured $35 million in construction financing from S3 Capital for Phase 3 of Casa Princeton in Princeton, Florida (Miami-Dade County). Phase 3 will deliver 162 apartments in an eight-story building. Phase 2, delivered in March 2026, comprises 150 units and is roughly 40 percent leased. The full community will total 374 units.
stories.impact: Phase 2's moderate 40% lease-up six months post-opening signals slower absorption and potential oversupply or underpricing in mid-market Miami-Dade attainable housing. Lender conviction on Phase 3 is noteworthy but conditional on Phase 2 performance. For developers: this flags Miami-Dade multifamily as moderately saturated in the $1,400–$1,800 rent band; new starts should focus on premium (Class A) or deeply affordable (LIHTC) segments. S3 Capital's willingness to finance Phase 3 suggests construction debt remains available, but cap rates on value-add product may be compressing.

stories.title: PPM America Provides $236M Acquisition Debt for 20-Property Industrial Deal
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between SparrowHawk and Almanac Realty Investors has secured $236 million in acquisition debt to buy a 4.4 million-square-foot, 20-property U.S. industrial portfolio, according to a release. Fidelity Investments reported earlier that the joint venture purchased the portfolio from EQT for just under $400 million. PPM America provided the $236 million debt, structured as a five-year, fixed-and-floating rate loan, while the JLL Capital Markets team of Brian Walsh, Lucas Borges, Steve Klein, Chris Pratt, Emma Berner and Christian Johnston arranged the transaction. JLL’s Walsh noted in a statement that SparrowHawk has “deep operational expertise” with industrial assets, while he described Almanac Realty Investors as an institutional player with “substantial capital resources.” “This transaction attracted significant lender interest given the institutional quality of the sponsorship and the portfolio’s strategic positioning across high-performing Midwest markets,” Walsh said. Known as “The Central Logistics Portfolio,” the 20-asset assemblage is located across six markets in four states — Kentucky, Ohio, Missouri and Illinois — and is 94 percent occupied by 30 logistics and distribution tenants specializing in different industries. The 20 buildings, on average, opened in 2006 and have an average building size of 221,000 square feet, while the portfolio itself is within a day’s drive of 50 percent of the U.S. population, due to its location in four Midwest states and cities Cincinnati, Columbus, Dayton, Louisville, Cleveland and St. Louis. bullets: PPM America provides $236M acquisition debt to SparrowHawk–Almanac JV for 20-property industrial portfolio.
Portfolio: 4.4M SF across Midwest; purchased from EQT for ~$400M; five-year fixed-and-floating structure.
JLL brokered transaction; lender praised sponsorship quality and portfolio's Midwest strategic positioning.
stories.summary: A joint venture between SparrowHawk and Almanac Realty Investors acquired a 4.4 million-square-foot, 20-property industrial portfolio from EQT for approximately $400 million. PPM America provided $236 million in acquisition debt structured as a five-year fixed-and-floating rate loan. JLL's Capital Markets team arranged the financing.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, institutional capital flowing to Midwest industrial and the sponsorship quality cited by lenders signals regional fundamentals (logistics, e-commerce, reshoring) remain solid. Midwest industrial demand strength indirectly supports local workforce housing demand, validating multifamily development in industrial hubs (Columbus, Indianapolis, Kansas City, Milwaukee). Tightness in high-quality industrial may drive developer attention to logistics-adjacent mixed-use and workforce housing.

stories.title: Nationwide Life Insurance Company Provides $51M Refi for D.C.-Area Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Zuckerman Gravely has secured $50.75 million to refinance Potomac Place Shopping Center, an 80,000-square-foot, Class-A grocery anchored retail center in Potomac, Md., a suburb just outside of Washington, D.C., Commercial Observer can first report. Nationwide Life Insurance Company provided the debt, structured as permanent fixed-rate financing with a seven-year term. Northmarq’s Jason Smith and Kenneth Gentzel arranged the transaction. In a statement, Smith described the asset as holding a strong retail base with long-time occupants that have generated “robust tenant sales” from a wealthy demographic cohort of residents from Potomac and nearby Chevy Chase and Bethesda, Md. “Located within the heart of Potomac, Maryland, Potomac Place Shopping Center is arguably the most valuable retail center in the region,” said Smith. Located at 10122 River Road in Potomac, near Route-90 and the Washington, D.C., beltway of Highway-495, Potomac Place Shopping Center opened in 1967. Current tenants include Safeway, Walgreens, Starbucks, Chipotle, M&T Bank and PNC Bank. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zuckerman Gravely refinances Potomac Place Shopping Center (80K SF, grocery-anchored) for $50.75M with Nationwide Life.
Seven-year permanent fixed-rate structure; Class-A center in Potomac, Md., opened 1967.
Tenants include Safeway, Walgreens, Starbucks; strong sales from affluent Potomac–Chevy Chase–Bethesda demographics.
stories.summary: Zuckerman Gravely refinanced Potomac Place Shopping Center, an 80,000-square-foot Class-A grocery-anchored retail center in Potomac, Maryland (D.C. suburb), with a $50.75 million permanent fixed-rate loan from Nationwide Life Insurance Company. The seven-year term reflects confidence in the center's long-term tenant stability and robust sales performance.
stories.impact: No direct impact on multifamily development. Retail refinancing at strong LTV in affluent D.C. suburb (Potomac) signals stable household wealth and discretionary spending, supporting mixed-use and experiential demand in the D.C. metro. Developers targeting premium multifamily in Potomac, Chevy Chase, or Bethesda can infer sustained rental demand from high-income demographics with strong retail sales metrics.

stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. bullets: Sytes (marketplace platform) connects landlords, developers, brokers with tenants seeking space in real-time.
Platform: 350+ tenants, 35K+ active listings across 50 states; clients include Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken.
Podcast features co-founder Rafael Weiss on tenant demand visibility, retail leasing inefficiency, and AI agents.
stories.summary: Sytes is a marketplace platform connecting commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively seeking space. Serving nearly 350 tenants and 35,000+ active listings across all 50 states, Sytes counts Kimco, InvenTrust, and national QSR chains as clients. A podcast with co-founder Rafael Weiss explores tenant demand visibility, leasing workflow, and the platform's impact on retail and mixed-use leasing.
stories.impact: Marginal multifamily relevance. Sytes targets retail and commercial leasing; however, the platform's success in surfacing tenant demand visibility suggests broader real estate data transparency is improving. For multifamily developers: lessons on demand forecasting, tenant preference aggregation, and AI-driven agent tools have secondary value in understanding emerging leasing-tech trends. No direct impact on apartment supply, demand, capital, or cost.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management (Barry Sternlicht) acquires two more Miami-Dade affordable properties for $51.6M total.
Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M) in Little River neighborhood.
Total acquisitions this week: $115.4M for 570 units (four deals); Freddie Mac financing backing both.
stories.summary: Starwood Asset Management purchased two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County: Lafayette Plaza (136 units) for $27 million and Emerald Terrace (124 units) for $24.6 million. Both are located in the Little River neighborhood and financed with Freddie Mac-backed loans via CBRE Capital Markets. Combined with two earlier acquisitions, Starwood has invested $115.4 million for 570 units in one week.
stories.impact: Major institutional capital (Starwood/Sternlicht) aggressively consolidating Miami-Dade affordable housing signals (1) strong conviction on tax-credit yields and Freddie Mac liquidity, (2) Little River and workforce housing submarkets attracting trophy-tier sponsors, and (3) affordability-focused product commanding institutional acquisition velocity. For developers: affordable and workforce housing in Miami-Dade faces consolidation by large players; new development projects must differentiate via tax-credit stacking, ground-lease creativity, or mixed-income hybrids. Competition for LIHTC equity and Agency financing will intensify; timing and capital structure now trump construction costs in underwriting feasibility.
